newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares slip on Dow, interest rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares slip on Dow, interest rate fears.

text.p: Russian stocks slipped on Monday on jitters over Wall Street's drop and fears of a possible rise in U.S. and German interest rates, traders said.

Traders said the Dow Jones index's 247-point fall on Friday, one of the biggest slides ever, affected the Russian market too, where stocks closed down overall, despite a late afternoon uptick on the Dow's firmer opening.
"The situation is unpredictable and all markets, not just ours, are in a mood of tense anticipation," said United City Bank's head of equity trading, Samit Yakovlev.
The Russian Trading System 21-share index closed down 3.28 percent to 544.69 after 563.14 on Friday. Total market turnover was a strong $90.2 million.
Traders did not see serious Western selling, but said support from domestic players was still not quite enough to hold the market up.
"Everyone is counting on broad Russian shoulders...but they are withstanding relatively small sales since there aren't any serious sellers," said United Financial Group trader Igor Vain.
"If sales increase, then it could all collapse."

National power company UES slipped to $0.4391 after Friday's closing $0.4495. Oil producer LUKoil eased to $27.10 after $27.86 and international long distance operator Rostelekom ticked down to $4.74 after $4.81.

Yakovlev said real market prices were even lower than rouble bids were showing, since Russian support was not supplying enough liquidity. But he said the market would take its cue from the Dow over the next few days.

"Right now, it is important to evaluate the longer term trend and in the light of that forecast investor behaviour -- will it be a big correction if there is a fall or just profit-taking?" Yakovlev said.
"We need to see how it closes and then draw our conclusions. If it really is a fall -- to under 7000 -- then of course Russia will not be able to avoid a sharp correction."
Vain said he thought a 10-15 percent correction was logical in the medium term, for which the behaviour of the Dow Jones index would simply be a pretext.
